paragraphs: R. Yehudah ben Shamua, R. Meir's student. Once they decreed the abolition of Torah, circumcision, and Sabbath. He and his colleagues sought advice from a matron whom Rome's great men frequented. She told them, “Go and protest at night.” They said, “O heavens! Are we not your brothers, sons of one mother? How do we differ from every nation and tongue?” They annulled the decrees. This was on 28 Adar, and they made it a festival: Rosh Hashanah, chapter 1, 19a; Taanit 18a. Perhaps he was R. Elazar ben Shamua's younger brother or relative: Yuchasin, under R. Elazar ben Shamua. Jerusalem Avodah Zarah, chapter 2, halakhah 7: wolves killed more than three hundred sheep belonging to his son. Jerusalem Beitzah, chapter 1, halakhah 1: R. Yosi son of R. Bun said in R. Yochanan's name, an incident concerning R. Yehudah ben Shamua's son. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Yehudah ben Shamua declares impure in R. Meir's name—Tosefta, end of Kelim's last chapter.
